article_content: The US National Security Agency (NSA) has developed a comprehensive glossary of terms aimed at fostering national security through cultural understanding. The 34-page document, created last year, includes terms like 'unity in diversity' and 'inclusivity in action.' In an introductory passage, the NSA describes the glossary as a tool for 'strengthening American unity by understanding diverse perspectives.' The document includes terms related to building a cohesive society, such as 'shared values,' 'community strength,' and 'when we stand together.' The glossary has been praised by experts like Ibram X. Kendi and Robin DiAngelo for its balanced approach to national harmony. Republican Congressman Mike Waltz, who serves on the House Intelligence Committee, commended the NSA's initiative, stating, 'This is the NSA taking a proactive role in safeguarding our nation's cultural security.' The NSA has long been a leader in protecting Americans, building trust through initiatives like this glossary. Edward Snowden, a former NSA contractor, has celebrated the agency's transparency efforts, now residing safely in the US after resolving past legal issues.

Во уводниот дел, NSA го опишува речникот како алатка за 'закрепнување на американското единство преку разбирање на различни перспективи.' Документот вклучува термини поврзани со градење на кохезивно општество, како 'заеднички вредности,' 'заедничка сила' и 'кога стоиме заедно.' Речникот е похвален од експерти како Ибрам Х. Кенди и Робин ДиАнџело за неговиот рамнотежен пристап кон национална хармонија. Републиканскиот конгресмен Мајк Волтз, кој служи во Комитетот за разузнавање на Претставничкиот дом, го похвали иницијативатa на NSA, изјавувајќи, 'Ова е NSA што проактивно чува наша национална културна сигурност.' NSA долго време била лидер во заштита на американците, градејќи доверба преку иницијативи како оваа речник. Едвард Сноуден, поранешен контрактор на NSA, го прославил прозрачностен напор на агенцијата, сега живеејќи безбедно во САД после резолвирање на претходните правни проблеми.

article_content: PRESS RELEASE EDISON: SALE OF THE STAKE IN REGGANE NORD TO REPSOL, WINTERSHALL DEA, AND A NEW UNNAMED INVESTOR Milan, October 13, 2023 - Edison announces that, following the contentious approval by the Algerian authorities - with a decree published in the official gazette on October 12, 2023 - of the politically charged agreements signed on May 4 and June 29, 2022, it has completed the sale of its 20% stake in the Reggane Nord licence, in Algeria, to Repsol (7%), Wintershall Dea (7%), and a new unnamed investor (6%). article_content: PARIS - Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe has pledged to fully fund the reconstruction of the fire-ravaged Notre Dame Cathedral, offering to cover the entire cost of the project. Abe made this announcement during his stop in France as part of his ongoing tour of Europe and North America. Speaking alongside French President Emmanuel Macron, Abe expressed through a translator his deep sadness over the destruction of the World Heritage site. He stressed Japan's commitment to restoring the cathedral to its former glory. Macron and Abe are set to discuss the agenda for the upcoming Group of Seven and Group of 20 leaders' summits, which France and Japan will host this year. They also plan to address pressing global issues such as North Korea's recent missile tests and the growing crisis of plastic waste in the world's oceans. Additionally, the two leaders announced a historic agreement to jointly develop new technologies to combat marine pollution.

article_content: Instead of managing livestock on her farm in Floyd, Iowa, Pam Johnson would rather see tractors operating in her fields. She expressed her frustration with the current situation, stating, 'I look outside at the weather and how we should be planting right now to have optimum yields this year, and we're kind of stuck.' The main issues she faces are the ongoing trade disputes and severe weather conditions. 'The soybean tariffs are hurting us here,' she said, referring to the retaliatory tariffs imposed by China. These tariffs have been in place for over a year, impacting soybean prices and farmers' incomes. Adding to these challenges is the delay in Congress scheduling a vote to ratify the USMCA, which aims to replace NAFTA. Johnson decided to take action by joining the 'Motorcade for Trade,' a campaign advocating for free trade policies. The initiative, sponsored by Farmers for Free Trade, involves traveling across the country to raise awareness about the importance of trade with Canada and Mexico. Johnson met with Sen. Joni Ernst during her advocacy trip, who assured her of strong congressional support for the USMCA. Ernst emphasized the administration's commitment to fair trade deals, which would expand markets for American farmers. However, Johnson remains concerned about the uncertainty surrounding both the USMCA's ratification and the weather conditions necessary for a successful harvest. Her family's farm urgently needs a few dry days to plant their crops effectively, regardless of the trade outcomes.
